subject: Application - Principal Software Engineer I, CI/CD (Platform Engineering Productivity)
paragraphs: I am applying for the Principal Software Engineer role on Platform Engineering Productivity. The description frames the job as making every engineering team ship faster and more securely, with leverage through the work of others, and that is the only kind of platform work I have done: this repo is the CI, the CD and the release process for a thirteen-host fleet, and the rule from the first commit is that a change is not finished until a gate has read the built artifact back.

The pipeline is hermetic by construction rather than by policy. Every input is pinned, every build happens in the Nix sandbox, and gates run with the builders switched off so a check can never quietly spend the build budget it is meant to protect. Sweeps that do need to build are dispatched one host per process under an out-of-memory watchdog, because an unbounded fleet sweep is how a CI box takes down the machine it is measuring. Deploys are single-writer by design: one host per process, no fleet-wide default, and a dry plan before any apply. Those gates are cheap to obey, which is why they are obeyed, and that is the property I would want to reproduce at Elastic scale.

The supply chain half of the description is where most of my recent work sits. Secrets are SOPS-encrypted per host with an age key cut from the host's SSH key, machines authenticate through a certificate authority instead of shared user keys, and self-hosted inputs are pinned so a host path cannot silently refetch different code. Vulnerability work is a scheduled pipeline over the CISA KEV catalogue matched against what the fleet actually runs, ordered by exposure and effort, so patching follows what is exploited. Content-addressed store paths give me provenance for free; the part that does not exist here is the org-wide policy layer that makes those guarantees legible to hundreds of engineers, and that is the part of this role I would be learning.

What I do not bring, stated plainly: no Buildkite, no Argo CD, and no production Kubernetes. Isolation here is a certificate authority and a module boundary rather than namespaces and quotas, GitOps is a flake and a task interface rather than a controller watching a cluster. I have also directed work without managing people: standards, design review and a task surface others adopt voluntarily, but not a team of engineers with quarterly goals. On location, the posting is for Poland and I am in Germany; I would rather ask whether a Germany contract exists than assume a relocation nobody has agreed to. On AI, I use coding agents as the operating layer of this fleet every day, including the checks and the coordination log, so the description's point about AI changing supply chain and scale is not abstract to me.
I would welcome a conversation about where the CI/CD roadmap is going and which bottleneck you would want addressed first.
